evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: eyebrow 'Cross-stitch patterns from photos', H1 'Your photo, stitched square by square.' and the lede ('turns a photo into a cross-stitch chart in real thread colours ... Fix a blotchy cheek, swap a thread you don't have') tell a hobbyist exactly what it is. Next step is muddied: the button says 'Open the beta editor' but actually scrolls to an on-page demo.
evidence.fit: Meets the core ask: the canvas is on the page and, beyond the brief, takes your own photo ('Your own photo...' chip; I uploaded a test PNG at 1440 and 390, toast 'Converted to 40 x 30 stitches using 9 threads'). Sellers get a full dark section 'Sell patterns? We haven't set commercial terms yet' with settled/undecided columns and an action. Footer and wb-foot state samples are 'drawn by us'. Weaknesses: the beta-editor main action is kept as a label it cannot fulfil; the seller section commits the founder to positions the brief has not taken ('Crossling doesn't claim anything over it', 'We will not quietly change this later').
evidence.distinctiveness: Linen-dotted background, serif display type, stitch-rendered X canvas, a thread-skein strip with real codes and a seller card make it feel like a craft product. Structure is still the familiar centred hero, three numbered step cards, FAQ accordion and centred final CTA band.
evidence.proof: The editor starts right under the hero (1440: toolbar visible at y~750, canvas below the fold). It is a real tool: Sailboat/Pear samples, brush/fill/pick/unpick, swap a thread everywhere ('Swapped 827 for 310 Black', palette counts updated), fabric count changes size (18-count: 3.4 x 3.4 cm), own-photo conversion, and 'Download chart as PNG' produced crossling-your-photo.png with symbols, 10-stitch guides and a thread key. This directly answers a hobbyist's first doubt ('will my photo work?').
evidence.craft: Polished at 1440 and 768 with deliberate type and colour. Defects: probe shows 68px horizontal overflow at 320 (header 'Open the beta editor' pill pushes to 388px, threads section follows); axe reports 17 serious colour-contrast nodes; thread-strip codes and 'beta' pill at 10.9px, stats labels 11.5px; toast at 1440 overlaps the canvas hint line.
evidence.mobile: 390: no navigation at all (.site-nav is display:none under 760px and there is no menu button), so 'For sellers' and 'FAQ' are only reachable by scrolling. First screen holds only the hero; the editor starts after one scroll. Toolbar collapses to unlabeled icon buttons at 36x36, Width/Threads selects are 29px tall, palette rows 33px, '+ Add a thread' 22px tall. Swap catalogue sits below the canvas so you cannot see the pattern change while you pick. Nothing overflows at 390.
evidence.honesty: Samples are labelled ('Both sample patterns are drawn by us'), and 'nothing is uploaded' sits under the hero CTA. But the primary 'Open the beta editor' (header, hero, final band) does not open a beta editor: it scrolls to the demo and only after the click shows a toast 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The FAQ contradicts that toast ('The editor on this page uses a short sample of the range ... the beta editor matches against the full catalogue'). 'Tell us what a seller plan needs' and footer 'Contact' go to mailto:hello@crossling.app, an address the brief never supplied. 'Free while in beta' and the beta's photo-retention policy are not in the brief.
evidence.interaction: At 1440 and 390 I operated: drag-brush, Fill, Undo, select a palette row then 'Swap for another thread' and a catalogue swatch, Stitches/Chart toggle, Pear sample, fabric select, photo upload, Download chart as PNG (file downloaded), Reset (toast 'Pattern reset'). All worked with zero console errors. Feedback is a bottom-centre toast that at 390 covers the thread list; CTA click moves focus to the canvas.
evidence.copy: Specific, customer-world language: 'drop the colour count before you buy floss', 'A chart is only useful if the shop sells the colour', 'the key you print is the shopping list you take to the store'. FAQ is useful ('Does it handle dark or low-contrast photos? Not magically.'). Docked for the toast/FAQ contradiction about whether the on-page editor is 'the real thing' and 'The ones we keep getting' implying a user base the brief says does not exist.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise and two buttons; the editor toolbar peeks at the very bottom but no pattern is visible, and the main button label does not match what it does. 390: hero text and buttons only, no artifact in view, and the 'Open the beta editor' label is the same mismatch.

problems: Primary action 'Open the beta editor' (header, hero, final band) does not open any beta editor: it scrolls to the on-page demo and explains only after the click via a toast, which itself contradicts the FAQ.
Seller and Contact actions mail hello@crossling.app, an address the brief did not supply; the seller section also commits the founder to IP and change-policy positions the brief has not decided.
Phone experience is thin: no navigation menu at all under 760px, icon-only 36px tools and 29px selects in the editor, artifact not in the first screen, 68px horizontal overflow at 320.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The most prominent first-screen action at 1440 is the red 'Open the beta editor' button (repeated in the header and the final band). Its label names a destination (the beta editor) that it does not reach: app.js CONFIG.BETA_URL is '' so the click handler calls preventDefault and scrolls to #editor on the same page, then shows a toast 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The page itself says the on-page editor is not the beta editor (FAQ 'Which threads does it use?': 'The editor on this page uses a short sample of the range ... the beta editor matches against the full catalogue'). Nothing before the click says the button only scrolls. This matches the rubric's 'label names a destination it does not reach ("Read the docs" that scrolls the page)'.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click the red hero button 'Open the beta editor'. The URL stays index.html, the page scrolls to 'Try it: a pattern you can edit' (scrollY 674) and the toast appears at the bottom. Repeat with the header button and the final 'Open the beta editor' button: same result. Then expand FAQ 'Which threads does it use?' to read that the on-page editor is a reduced sample, not the beta editor.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Turn a photo into a cross-stitch pattern, then change any stitch.' plus 'Crossling is a pattern editor for cross-stitchers ... charts the picture in real thread colours you can edit square by square' says what, for whom and how; the button 'Try the sample editor' says exactly what happens next. Readable the same way at 390.
evidence.fit: On-page editing and recolouring are central (editor beside the H1 at 1440). Original artwork stated twice ('Sample only: the source is a drawing, not a photo'; footer 'The pear is original artwork drawn for this page'). The missing beta address is resolved deliberately: the CTA is renamed 'Try the sample editor' and the final band says 'its link will sit here when it does'. Commercial use is stated as undecided in the seller column and the pricing list. Gaps: the seller audience gets one column and a note with no way to express interest, and a hobbyist cannot try their own photo on the page at all.
evidence.distinctiveness: Split hero with the live editor as the hero image, and a 'same picture at 12, 22 and 40 stitches across' section with real centimetre sizes are product-specific. The overall look (grey ground, Avant-Garde-style display, boxed sections, three-step row) is clean but closer to a generic Swiss template.
evidence.proof: 1440: an operable 22x22 pear editor is in the first viewport. I stitched by drag (status 'Stitched row 7, column 7 in 433 Medium brown.'), swapped colours ('Swapped 40 stitches of 734 Light olive green for 433 Medium brown.'), re-charted at 4 and 10 threads, added a catalogue thread, unpicked, undid and started over; thread list counts and '22 x 22 stitches: 4.0 x 4.0 cm on 14-count aida' update. Sizes and how-it-works sections are rendered by the same code from the same drawing. Missing: no own-photo trial and no chart export, so 'will my photo look good?' stays unanswered.
evidence.craft: Probe: axe 0 violations, smallest text 13px, no overflow at 320 or 390, no errors. Consistent spacing and strong hierarchy at 1440/768/390. Plain rather than crafted; at 390 the editor becomes a long column (grid, tools, 11 swatches, catalogue, 11-row thread list) before the status line.
evidence.mobile: 390: 'Menu' button opens a full list incl. 'Try the sample editor', Escape closes it, links close it and scroll. First screen shows H1, lead, CTA and the editor header with Stitches/Chart and 4/7/10 controls; the grid begins at the fold. Tool buttons labelled ('Stitch', 'Swap colour', 'Unpick') at 40px tall, swatches 36x36 (under 44). The status message sits at the bottom of the editor, well below the grid, so text feedback is out of view while tapping (the grid itself does change).
evidence.honesty: Every example labelled where it appears ('Sample pattern, 22 x 22 stitches', 'Sample only: the source is a drawing, not a photo. The beta editor takes your own photos.', 'Counts come from this sample', 'shades on screen are approximate'). The CTA says what will happen before you click. Commercial use stated as 'Not decided'. Not from the brief: 'The beta is free to use while pricing is worked out ... nothing will be charged before that'.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440 and 390: Stitch, Swap colour, Unpick, Undo, Start over, Stitches/Chart, 4/7/10 thread counts (re-chart says 'Your edits were cleared; Undo brings them back'), More threads from the catalogue, mobile menu with Escape. All worked, no console errors, status messages are specific. Fewer capabilities than A: no photo input, no export, no fill tool.
evidence.copy: Plain and specific: 'For the photo on your fridge, and for the patterns you sell', 'A stem, an eye, a whisker: averages lose small things.', 'Fewer stitches means a quicker, blockier piece; more means detail and a longer evening.' Button text matches outcomes. Slightly dry, and 'The sample is the real engine' is an unverifiable claim.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: one viewport holds a specific promise, the honest CTA, and the operable editor with thread list and finished size. 390: promise, CTA and 'no account, nothing uploaded' are in view, the editor card header is visible but the stitch grid only starts at the fold.

problems: The demo is a fixed drawn pear: a hobbyist cannot try their own photo or export a chart, so the product's core promise (photo to pattern) is shown only on a drawing.
Pattern sellers, the likelier payers, get one column and a 'not settled yet' note with no way to register interest or ask the question.
On a phone the editor is a long single column: text feedback (status line) sits below the swatches and thread list, far from the grid, and swatches are 36px targets.

reason: As the founder I could put B live tomorrow: every label and its main action do what they say, the editor is in the first screen, and nothing commits me to an address or seller terms I have not decided. A is the more compelling product demo for a hobbyist (own-photo upload and a printable chart download), but its main button promises a beta editor it cannot open, and it mails an address the brief never gave. If A's main button were relabelled to match the scroll and the seller path used a supplied contact, A's photo upload and export would likely win me over.
